scope: Nine pull requests, one review each. A screen, not a leaderboard: flash-class recall swings by about two known issues between identical runs, so do not generalize a single row.

model.route: OpenCode Zen free tier, $0 per token while the free window lasts
model.catalog: models.dev lists a 1,000,000-token context, 65,536 output tokens, text, image and video input, effort low, medium or high, release date 2026-09-16

setup.reviewer: J-Bot Review local mode; Step 5 runs at jbot-review 0906459 with OpenCode 2.0.24; verification off, 10 concurrent sessions, one run per pull request
setup.comparison: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (deepseek/deepseek-flash on the direct DeepSeek API)

definitions.pages: Review pages: J-Bot splits a diff into budgeted pages, and every page must finish before a review posts.
definitions.known_issues: Issues in an audit answer key written before these runs. Findings were matched to the key by keyword, and every unmatched finding was checked by hand.
definitions.failed: The review hit its 30-minute budget without every page finishing, so J-Bot posted nothing.

public_pr.known_issues_source: The two shell-parsing bugs fixed afterwards in https://github.com/pgup-ai/jbot-review/pull/287
public_pr.telemetry_bug: A telemetry helper gained a workspace parameter that three backend call sites did not pass. Step 5 named all three call sites. Fixed in https://github.com/pgup-ai/jbot-review/pull/293

private_prs.source: Eight production pull requests from one private TypeScript monorepo, labelled A to H

runs.failure: One page returned an empty response and its retry ran out the budget
One page ended with a partial result

completed_summary.speed_note: No general speed multiplier: only #286, A and B have a DeepSeek time, all from older J-Bot code. Step 5 was 1.9x slower on #286 and A and faster on B.

deepseek_reference.note: Older J-Bot code, so a rough comparison. No DeepSeek run was paired on C to H.
